headline: OSB price collapse drives steep annual decline
summary_short: Q1 FY2026 revenue fell 20.7% y/y to $574M (up 1.2% q/q) as OSB net sales dropped 37% on 21-31% lower prices, while net income fell 70.3% y/y to $27M and diluted EPS fell 70.0% y/y to $0.39; OSB segment Adjusted EBITDA swung to a $12M loss from $54M a year ago.
summary_long: Revenue fell 20.7% y/y to $574M as OSB net sales dropped 37% to $168M on 21-31% lower prices, while Siding fell 10% to $360M despite a 9% price increase, on an 18% volume drop. OSB Adjusted EBITDA swung to a $12M loss from $54M; Siding Adjusted EBITDA fell 5% to $101M as pricing gains were outweighed by volume declines. Net income fell 70.3% y/y to $27M ($0.39 diluted EPS, $0.38 adjusted). Operating cash flow swung to -$38M on lower income and working capital; cash fell to $164M from $292M after $61M capex and $21M dividends. FY2026 capex guided to ~$390M.

drivers.explanation: OSB net sales fell 37% on materially lower average selling prices (Structural Solutions -21%, Commodity -31%) and lower volumes; Siding net sales fell 10% as a 9% price increase was outweighed by an 18% volume decline.
Gross profit fell in line with the OSB and Siding net-sales declines; cost of sales fell only 12.7% against a 20.7% revenue decline, so gross margin compressed year over year.

Income from operations fell mainly on OSB segment Adjusted EBITDA falling $66M on lower prices and volumes, and Siding Adjusted EBITDA falling $5M as pricing gains of $27M were more than offset by $35M of lower volumes.
Company Adjusted EBITDA fell to $82M from $162M, reflecting the OSB segment swing to a loss and a smaller Siding and Other-segment decline described above.

Net income fell in step with lower operating income, partly offset by a smaller net non-operating loss ($3M gain vs $5M loss a year ago) and a lower tax provision; effective tax rate rose to 25% from 22% on the absence of a prior-year discrete tax benefit.
EPS fell in step with net income; diluted share count was flat at 70M in both periods, so per-share and aggregate net income moved together.
Cash from operations swung to a $38M outflow primarily on lower net income and changes in working capital, per the filing; inventories built $51M and payables fell $33M in the quarter.

Single-family housing starts fell 6% y/y while multi-family rose 19%; OSB commodity price weakness drove that segment to an Adjusted EBITDA loss for the first time in this window, while Siding held closer to prior-year profitability despite lower volumes.
